drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Full Match | Two rucks, wide try
drills.players: 16 children: 8 attackers (A1–A8) and 8 defenders (D1–D8), plus a qualified coach/referee supervising off the field. Attack towards the upper goal line. All roles rotate between repetitions.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball, correctly marked 60 × 35 m U10 field with 5 m in-goal at each end; cones if marking a temporary field. Safe surface and adequate run-offs.
drills.objective: Use two safe U10 breakdowns and connected support to create a wide scoring opportunity on a fully marked 60 × 35 m pitch.
drills.instructions:
01. Full field · eight against eight — Eight attackers and eight defenders are set on a marked U10 pitch (60 × 35 m plus in-goal). Attack moves towards the upper goal line. Players hold supporting depth; no coach joins play.
02. Pass from link · A1 to A2 — A1 releases backwards to A2. The receiver stays behind the passer at release, then straightens upfield.
03. Short pass to a straight runner — A2 squares up, draws a defender and passes backwards to A3. A4 tracks on the support side.
04. Carry · engage the defensive line — A3 carries directly towards D3. Defenders advance within their channels; support stays behind the ball.
05. Controlled tackle · both go to ground — D3 completes an age-grade appropriate controlled tackle. A3 goes to ground and must make the ball available. This is a phase-play schematic, not a tackle-technique demonstration.
06. Release · clear the tackle — D3 releases the ball carrier and moves away. A3 remains grounded and prepares to present back towards their own team.
07. Present ball towards support — A3 places the ball back on the attacking side without throwing or squeezing it. A4 arrives from behind and stays on their feet.
08. U10 ruck · one support player per side — A4 and D4 meet upright over the grounded ball, one arriving player per side. Other players stay behind their team's hindmost feet. Dashed guide lines are schematic, not a substitute for judging real feet.
09. Secure ball · play it away — The attacking side secures the ball. The link waits on the attacking side and plays it away promptly once available. The ruck is not a place for extra players to join.
10. A1 collects available ball at the back — A1 takes the available ball on the attacking side after the contest and prepares to pass. Supporting receivers stay behind the ball at release.
11. Pass from the breakdown to A5 — A1 passes backwards to A5. A5 runs square before committing the second line of defence.
12. A5 commits · passes to A6 — A5 carries forward, fixes D5 and releases a short backward pass to A6, who follows on a straight support line.
13. Second carry · A6 takes contact — A6 carries into the next channel while A7 and A8 stay wider. D6 approaches for a controlled contact phase.
14. Second controlled tackle — D6 completes the second controlled tackle. A6 goes to ground and protects against dangerous handling or extra players entering the contest.
15. Release and present · phase two — D6 releases and clears. A6 presents back towards their own support. A5 tracks the ball but does not enter illegally.
16. Ruck again · back-feet offside — A4 and D5 are the one-on-one arriving contest over the ball; D6 is clear. Both supporting lines stay onside while the ball is secured.
17. Use it · ready to switch play — The ball is available behind the ruck. A1 takes the linking role. No extra attacker joins the ruck.
18. A1 takes possession · scan wide — A1 collects the secured ball behind the contest. Outside supporters hold width and depth; the defence remains narrow around the ruck.
19. Pass A1 to A7 · attack the edge — A1 releases a backward pass to A7. D7 is drawn towards the receiver; A8 stays behind ready for the next pass.
20. A7 draws D7 · release to A8 — A7 straightens towards D7, then passes backwards to A8. The receiver takes the ball behind A7, before accelerating into the outside lane.
21. A8 breaks into open space — A8 runs up the outside channel, staying inside touch. Defensive cover chases from behind, but cannot reach the carrier.
22. Cross, ground and score — A8 crosses the attacking goal line while carrying the ball, then deliberately grounds it in the in-goal area. Crossing alone is not a try.
23. Hold in-goal · celebrate and review — A8 stays at the exact grounding position. The scoring celebration never reverses through the goal line. Review how two legal breakdowns created the wide opportunity.
drills.coaching: Straighten before passing; keep receivers behind the ball; support close enough to secure a tackle without crowding; release and present after contact; one on-foot support contest per team at a U10 ruck; keep non-participants behind the hindmost feet; move the secured ball away quickly; ground deliberately in-goal.
drills.safety: Educational phase-play animation only. RFU U10 2026–27: maximum eight players per side, maximum 60 × 35 m field plus 5 m in-goal, size-4 ball, modified contact, rucks with a strictly limited contest. Rucks use a maximum of one arriving support player from each team (two players per side including the tackled carrier or tackler in the illustrative contact picture). Tacklers release promptly; all other players stay behind their own hindmost feet. No hand-offs, kicking, head-first contact or jumping over rucks. This diagram is NOT a technique lesson or a substitute for RFU TackleSafe and qualified age-grade coaching. Coaches should review the current official age-grade appendix, supervise physical contact and assess readiness. Current U10 guidance requires tackles at sternum/belly height or below, prohibits hand-offs/fending, and forbids a carrier deliberately dipping the head into the tackle. When the referee calls 'use it' after the ball is secured, the team must play it away within five seconds. Never coach children to drive through or over grounded players.
drills.regression: Start with walking-speed, conditioned touch defence and a single tackle-present-recycle. Pause to identify who may join the contest and where the offside lines lie.
drills.progression: Increase defensive realism within U10 rules; freeze at each breakdown to explain release, the permitted one-on-one support contest and onside positioning; challenge players to recognise the space before the final pass.
drills.questions: Who is behind the ball at each pass? Does the tackler release? Which player may join the U10 ruck? Where is each team's back-foot offside line? What changed in the defence? What makes the final grounding a try? What should players do when the referee calls 'use it'?

The video-length animation uses deliberate, readable teaching pauses. Steps are visual story beats, not prescribed timings for a training session. Camera: full field for setup, follow action for the phase, wider at the finish. Captions appear only at teaching moments; one short callout per cue. branching.question: The defence is drifting. Is the space outside or on the inside shoulder?
branching.context: Both animated options begin from precisely the same frozen position after the first ruck. D6's next movement determines the best attacking choice.
branching.watchFor: If D6 compresses, pass to the edge. If D6 drifts wide, find the inside support runner. Pass backwards in either case.

choices.label: Defence compresses · use width
choices.explanation: D6 follows the carrier inside, creating a numerical advantage for A8 on the edge.
choices.watchFor: A5 → A6 → A7 → A8; every pass is backwards, then A8 grounds the wide try.

frames.name: A · hold and review
frames.notes: The winger stays in-goal after scoring. Discuss what D6 did to create the overlap.

choices.label: Defence drifts · hit inside support
choices.explanation: D6 slides outside, leaving a central running channel for A4 arriving from behind.
choices.watchFor: A5 straightens, makes a short backward inside pass to A4 and A4 grounds a central try.

frames.name: B · D6 drifts early to the outside
frames.notes: D6 slides wide towards A6 and A7, leaving the inside shoulder for a support runner.

frames.name: B · A5 shapes wide, then holds square
frames.notes: A5 keeps the defender committed to the drift, without throwing a forward or obstructive pass.

frames.name: B · short inside support pass
frames.notes: A5 gives a backwards short pass to A4 running an inside support line from behind the ball.

frames.name: B · support runner breaks centrally
frames.notes: A4 cuts into the uncovered central gap, accelerates past the drifting defenders and carries towards the line.

frames.name: B · central try · deliberate grounding
frames.notes: A4 crosses the designated attacking goal line and grounds inside the in-goal area, with the ball still in possession.

frames.name: B · hold and review
frames.notes: A4 stays in-goal and celebrates. Discuss why the drifting defender left the inside gap.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Close Range | Patient phases, central try
drills.players: 16 children: 8 attackers (A1–A8) and 8 defenders (D1–D8), plus a qualified coach/referee supervising off the field. Attack towards the upper goal line. All roles rotate between repetitions.
drills.equipment: One size-4 rugby ball, correctly marked 60 × 35 m U10 field with 5 m in-goal at each end; cones if marking a temporary field. Safe surface and adequate run-offs.
drills.objective: Recycle patiently after two tackles and rucks; spot an inside support lane and finish with a grounded central try.
drills.instructions:
01. U10 field · play from a near-line phase — Eight attackers and eight defenders use a marked U10 pitch. The first contact occurs in the attacking half; this is a progression demonstration, not a full match restart.
02. Link pass to first receiver — A1 passes backwards to A2. Support runners follow behind the ball.
03. First short carry to A3 — A2 moves up and passes behind to A3 for a straight midfield carry.
04. Carry into the first tackle — A3 advances with a balanced body position, no hand-off. D3 closes on the carrier.
05. Controlled tackle · hold safely — D3 brings A3 to the ground in the schematic. Contact technique requires qualified coaching, not this animation.
06. Release · ball back to your team — D3 promptly releases and leaves the tackle. A3 makes a clear presentation back towards support.
07. U10 ruck · one arrives on each side — Only A4 and D4 join the upright contest. Other players stay out and remain onside behind the hindmost feet.
08. Quick ball · A1 ready behind — The ball is secured and ready to be played away promptly. A1 positions to link the next phase.
09. A1 picks up and passes to A5 — A1 collects and passes to A5 behind the ball, avoiding a pick-and-go into a crowded breakdown.
10. A5 makes a straight short carry — A5 attacks the gap between D5 and D6; the defence closes and A6 stays behind as support.
11. Second tackle · controlled contact — D5 completes the tackle and must release. The attacking team does not pile extra players onto the contest.
12. Release and present towards A6 — A5 presents back as D5 clears. A6 stays on feet and prepares to support from the attacking side.
13. Short ruck · guard the ball — A6 and D6 form the upright one-on-one arriving contest; no additional ruck entrants. The defensive guard stays behind the last feet.
14. Use it · look at the fringe — A1 waits until the ball is available. D7 drifts towards width, leaving space next to the ruck.
15. A1 collects · passes short to A7 — Rather than diving over bodies, A1 passes a short backward ball to A7, who takes a support line into space.
16. A7 breaks outside the ruck — A7 runs directly through the unguarded channel with A8 available outside. Cover defenders turn to chase.
17. A7 crosses and grounds centrally — A7 carries across the opposition goal line and grounds the ball inside in-goal. The ball is deliberately placed down to score.
18. Hold the score · review pressure — A7 remains inside in-goal after grounding. Review how support, legal recycling and one good pass created the close-range finish.

frames.name: Hold the score · review pressure
frames.notes: A7 remains inside in-goal after grounding. Review how support, legal recycling and one good pass created the close-range finish.
